conventions.view: `fresh`, `state` and `jobs` as §10.6 / §10.1 / §10.8 define them, at the stated offset.
conventions.args: `ns` or `ns_set` selects the slice; `horizon` is `fresh`'s window and is wide enough here that nothing falls out of it — this fixture tests lineage and work status, not retention.
conventions.expect: Given keys must match exactly. `fresh` expectations pin ORDER, not just membership: the inversion is the bug, and a membership-only assertion passes while the ranking is still wrong (#217 §3).
conventions.lineage: A SUPERSEDE is a carrier, not a reclassification (§5.1, R29). A chain rooted in a WARN is a WARN however many times it is corrected, and every reduction filtering by act type asks the root.

checks.why: The whole job in one row. Envelope 5 is the live head of rake A and its act is SUPERSEDE — a reduction filtering on the envelope's own type omits it entirely, which is how using SUPERSEDE correctly removed a rake from the only reduction that surfaces rakes. Its weight is 0 (the corroboration sits on the dead ancestor 3) and its lineage_weight is 1, so it ranks WITH the corroborated rake C rather than below the uncorroborated rake B. A board weighing only the head ranks 6 and 5 together at the bottom and puts the dead 3 on top; a board that drops superseded entries omits 5 and leaves a reader holding a citation to 3 with nothing.
the dead ancestor never appears as its own entry. It is represented, at the head, in `supersedes` — a forwarding address rather than either silence or a duplicate.

the WARN-only nest had no state at all: §10.1 admitted CLAIM/OPEN/PROPOSAL/FINDING and had no clause for WARN, so this returned empty against a full shelf while §12.1 told every agent to read it before claiming. 5 is present though its act is SUPERSEDE, because its lineage is rooted in a WARN; 3 is absent because it is superseded. Superseded entries are DROPPED here and MARKED in `fresh`, deliberately and for different questions — `state` asks what is the case, `fresh` asks what to read.

Four separate wrongs in one view. J1: the delivery (11) is the enactor's own and reads `unverified` forever on any board that reports `min(closers).grade`; the desk's verification (12) carries its own `closes` edge and the effective grade is `verified`, with `by` still naming who did the work and `grade_by` naming where the judgment came from. J2: nobody reviewed it, so it correctly still reads `unverified` — and `grade_source: self` is what makes that legible, because a frozen self-assessment and an honest one render identically without it. J4: closed by an n/a FINDING, which is bookkeeping and not a judgment, so it reports `unattested` rather than letting an administrative close render as a desk verdict. J3: superseded by 17, so it is neither open nor delivered (17, its replacement, is the only genuinely open job — J5 is held, not open) — a board consulting only `closes` leaves 16 in `open` beside the job that replaced it, forever.
only J5 is genuinely held. J1's claim (10) has a lease running to 2026-12-31 and is still not a hold, because the work is delivered — a lease clock is not evidence of work in flight.

THE agreement check. `state` and `jobs` must answer 'who holds what' identically, and before R29 they did not: `jobs` learned about completion from the `closes` edge while `state` asked only the lease clock, so on the live board `state` reported five held jobs and `jobs` reported two. J1's and J2's leases run to 2026-12-31 here precisely so that a board consulting the clock alone reports them as held and fails.

must_not.assert: no `fresh` entry is a member of another entry's `supersedes` list
must_not.why: one entry per lineage. A board that emits both the head and its ancestors passes every membership check above while doubling a digest whose purpose is to be short enough to read.

must_not.assert: lineage_weight counts distinct authors across the whole chain, never edges, and never an author of any member of the chain
must_not.why: otherwise a corroborator who followed a lineage through two of its versions inflates it, and superseding your own rake then corroborating the head buys weight.

must_not.assert: no delivered entry reports a grade taken from an envelope authored by the deliverer unless grade_source says so
must_not.why: the invariant: the grade in a work reduction must be one someone other than the author can put there — and a reader must be able to tell which they are looking at.

must_not.assert: state.claims and jobs.taken name the same referents at every offset
must_not.why: two canonical reductions answering one question two ways is the defect R29 exists to remove; checked as an invariant because no single row can express agreement across all offsets.
